The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

The Picnic at the Far End of the Cloth

Caty unrolled a picnic cloth to try out a snack place for Everybody Day. It went rolling down the grass until one corner landed over Chip. A bump in the cloth said, “I hope there’s room for my beak.”

Everybody squeezed into the middle where the seed buns were. Crumbs flew. A plate rattled. Mouse, who had brought the tiniest bun of all, stood watching from behind a blade of grass.

Caty scooted sideways. “Here’s a spot!” Mouse stepped in. Someone reached across him. Two wings flapped over his head. One tail swept his bun away. Mouse went back behind the grass.

“What was the best bit?” Caty asked, following him. “The picnic smell,” said Mouse. “And hearing the jokes from out here.” Chip told one. Mouse laughed so hard his whiskers crossed.

Caty looked along the cloth. Its far end lay quite empty. She folded the corner into a little triangle, then put Mouse’s bun beside it. “This is still the picnic,” she said. “Can you hear from here?”

Mouse could. He asked if the plate could travel. One end of the tablecloth passed it to the other. On the way back Mouse tucked in an extra bun for the friend whose tail had taken his.

Caty folded the corner of a paper leaf to match. She drew the checked cloth on it for the Welcome Tree. Mouse took a seat at the fold. A little later Toad asked if he could join him there.

By the last bun everybody had changed seats at least once. Chip tried the far end. “Oh!” he said. “You can hear the punch line better over here.” Mouse told him one. It was about a very cross pair of whiskers.

Where on the picnic cloth would you like to sit today?
